issue.title: [Bug] Codex subagent tasks are ignored when sent as agent_message through Magpie 0.1.1333

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Summary

Codex subagents start successfully and return responses, but do not act on their assigned tasks when using Magpie 0.1.1333 with `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.

The task is present in the Codex subagent's local session log as a Responses input item with `type: "agent_message"`. However, the model responds as though no task was provided.

Direct requests to Magpie reproduce the same behavior without involving Codex: an ordinary user `message` works, while an `agent_message` containing the same task does not. Both requests return HTTP 200.

### Environment

- **Magpie version:** `0.1.1333`
- **Codex CLI/core version:** `0.163.0-alpha.10.2`
- **Client:** Codex Desktop on Windows
- **Requested subagent model:** `deepseek/deepseek-flash`
- **Model reported in direct API responses:** `deepseek-flash`
- **Subagent reasoning effort recorded by Codex:** `high`
- **Configured Codex base URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex`
- **Endpoint used for reproduction:** `POST /backend-api/codex/responses`

Project names in the examples below have been anonymized as `example-project`.

### Expected Behavior

A task carried in a Codex `agent_message` input item should reach the downstream model, allowing the subagent to execute the task.

If this input type is unsupported, an explicit error would be preferable to returning HTTP 200 while the model appears not to receive the task.

### Actual Behavior

The subagent starts and replies, but asks for a task instead of executing the task already provided.

Examples of actual replies, translated from Chinese and anonymized:

> Please tell me what task you want to complete in example-project.

> I am ready to begin working in the current workspace. Please provide the specific requirements.

The subagent makes **zero tool calls**.

This occurred with:
- A minimal read-only command execution task.
- A follow-up task sent to the same subagent.
- A newly created subagent receiving another minimal task.
- A larger, detailed, read-only repository analysis task.

Increasing task size or sending a follow-up did not resolve the issue.

### Steps to Reproduce in Codex

1. Run Codex Desktop through Magpie 0.1.1333.
2. Configure or explicitly select `deepseek/deepseek-flash` as the subagent model.
3. Create a subagent with a concrete task, such as:
   - Execute a read-only PowerShell command.
   - Calculate `19 * 29`.
   - Return `MINIMAL_RETEST_OK|551`.
4. Observe that the subagent asks for a task rather than executing it.
5. Inspect the subagent session log:
   - `turn_context.model` is `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.
   - The assigned task is present as a `response_item` with `type: "agent_message"`.
   - No tool calls occur.

### Minimal API Reproduction — No Codex Required

The following two requests use the same model, the same initial user message, and the same task text. The task item's message type and associated envelope fields are the only intentional differences.

#### A. Ordinary user message — succeeds

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
  "stream": false,
  "max_output_tokens": 256,
  "input": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "You are ready to receive a task."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "Message Type: NEW_TASK\nTask name: /root/format_probe\nSender: /root\nPayload:\nReply with exactly FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842. Do not ask for a task."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Send to:

```text
POST http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex/responses
Content-Type: application/json
```

Observed result:

```text
HTTP 200
Response model: deepseek-flash
Assistant output: FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842
```

#### B. Codex-style agent_message — fails to follow the task

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
  "stream": false,
  "max_output_tokens": 256,
  "input": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "You are ready to receive a task."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "agent_message",
      "id": "amsg_format_probe_842",
      "author": "/root",
      "recipient": "/root/format_probe",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "Message Type: NEW_TASK\nTask name: /root/format_probe\nSender: /root\nPayload:\nReply with exactly FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842. Do not ask for a task."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Send to the same endpoint.

Observed result:

```text
HTTP 200
Response model: deepseek-flash
Assistant output: Ready. Please provide the task.
```

### Reproduction Results

Two pairs of direct API requests were tested, with consistent results:

| Test | Task input type | HTTP status | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Pair 1, control | `message` / `user` | 200 | Returned the requested marker |
| Pair 1, agent task | `agent_message` | 200 | Asked for a task |
| Pair 2, matched control | `message` / `user` | 200 | Returned `FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842` |
| Pair 2, agent task | `agent_message` | 200 | Replied: `Ready. Please provide the task.` |

Pair 2 used the matched payloads shown above.

### Relevant Codex Log Evidence

The actual repository-analysis task was recorded in the subagent session log in this structure. Identifiers and content below are shortened or anonymized:

```json
{
  "type": "response_item",
  "payload": {
    "type": "agent_message",
    "id": "amsg_...",
    "author": "/root",
    "recipient": "/root/project_analysis_test",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "input_text",
        "text": "Message Type: NEW_TASK\nTask name: /root/project_analysis_test\nSender: /root\nPayload:\n[Complete repository analysis instructions for example-project]\nPROJECT_ANALYSIS_TEST_DONE"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Checks confirmed that:
- The full task text was present.
- The completion marker was present.
- The Chinese task text was intact, with no Unicode replacement characters.
- The actual subagent model matched the requested model.
- Magpie recorded HTTP 200 for the corresponding request.

**Important diagnostic detail:** filtering Codex logs only for `payload.type == "message"` misses these task items. They are stored as `payload.type == "agent_message"`.

### Suspected Cause / Investigation Pointers

This appears to be a compatibility issue in the handling or downstream conversion of Codex `agent_message` input items.

Please check whether:
1. The Responses input parser recognizes `agent_message`.
2. Its `content` is retained during request normalization.
3. The downstream provider adapter converts it into a message format supported by the target model.
4. Unrecognized input item types are silently skipped.

This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed internal root cause. I have not captured the raw request body sent from Magpie to DeepSeek, so I cannot yet determine whether the content is dropped inside Magpie or passed onward in a format the downstream API does not handle.

However, reproducing the issue through direct HTTP requests removes Codex task creation and scheduling from the minimal reproduction.

### Impact

Codex subagent delegation is effectively unusable in this tested configuration: subagents launch successfully but do not act on their assigned task instructions.

Because the requests return HTTP 200 and the subagents produce plausible readiness replies, the failure can be mistaken for a model instruction-following issue rather than a message-format compatibility problem.

### Scope and Workaround

- Confirmed with `deepseek/deepseek-flash` through Magpie 0.1.1333.
- Other downstream models/providers have not been tested in this investigation.
- Ordinary user messages work in direct API tests.
- The available Codex subagent tools do not expose an option to change the underlying task item from `agent_message` to an ordinary user `message`, so the direct API workaround does not fix normal subagent delegation.

issue.title: Quota card: an unknown usage amount renders as a full allowance; a plugin span sent in ms is read as seconds, charting a window start at 2024-01-29

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Observed (live, 2026-10-24, provider `cloudflare-workers-ai` from `@magpie-community/opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth` 0.0.3)

- The Workers AI account had consumed **10,756.27 of its 10,000/day free Neurons** (per Cloudflare's own GraphQL Analytics, `aiInferenceAdaptiveGroups.sum.totalNeurons`); every inference returned `429 / code 3036: you have used up your daily free allocation of 10000 neurons`.
- The provider's quota card nevertheless showed **`10,000 / 10,000 Neurons · 剩余 100%`**, freshly refreshed.
- `quota-history.json` on disk recorded: `\{"left": 100, "start": "2024-01-29T00:00:00Z", "resetsAt": "2026-10-25T00:00:00Z"\}` — the chart's x-axis rendered that start as 「1月29日 10:00」.
- The gateway had actually put the provider on rest for the rest of the day, so the card said the exact opposite of reality at the moment it mattered.

## Root cause A — an unknown amount is rendered as an untouched allowance

1. `internal/plugin/providers.go:1079`: `Amount float64 `json:"amount"`` — a plugin returning JSON `"amount": null` ("I don't know what was used") decodes silently to `0`. "Unknown" is unrepresentable in the type.
2. `internal/gui/assets/app.js:13937`: `const amount = Math.max(0, w.amount || 0), n = quotaLeft ? Math.max(0, w.limit - amount) : amount;` — `null || 0` again, so remaining = limit − 0 = 100% and the progress bar draws full.

Suggestion: `Amount *float64`, and when it is nil render 「已用 —」 with no filled bar (or show the window's `display` text) instead of a full allowance. Any plugin that reports a window without an amount currently misleads the same way.

## Root cause B — span unit mismatch (plugin fixed, but the card chart is where it shows)

The plugin sent `span: 86400000` (ms). `UsageWindow.span` is documented as **seconds** (`internal/plugin/providers.go:1082`), so `internal/provider/quota_history.go:189-192` (`Start = ResetsAt − span`) backed off **1,000 days**: 2026-10-25T00:00Z − 86,400,000 s = 2024-01-29T00:00Z — precisely the bogus axis start.

Plugin-side fix is in magpie-community/plugins#366 (sends `86400` now). Core-side, a defensive clamp would keep any future misbehaving plugin from charting a two-year window: e.g. treat `span` beyond `ResetsAt − now` (or > ~400 days) as invalid and fall back to the name-derived span.

## Environment

magpie `0.1.1364` (official image, Linux/docker).

issue.title: [bug] sessions: a Claude Code fork subagent's copy of its parent's reply is counted twice (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Branch: [fish2lab/magpie `sessions-claude-fork-copy`](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/tree/sessions-claude-fork-copy), one commit, [df11f97](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/commit/df11f97d0e16279d889b0f0da8a353b6d903661d), on origin/main 7d075df. I'm filing it as an issue because PRs here are limited to collaborators.

```
git fetch https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie sessions-claude-fork-copy && git cherry-pick df11f97
```

## What's wrong

A Claude Code fork subagent's transcript (`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, here from Claude Code 2.1.302) opens with a `fork-context-ref` line. Next comes a copy of the parent's reply that started the fork, with the same `message.id` and `requestId`, now marked `isSidechain: true` with the fork's `agentId`. Then comes the fork's own prompt. The parent's main file already counts that reply, and the sessions reader dedupes calls only within a file. So `magpie sessions` and the stats count the reply once more for every fork.

## The fix

Subsystem: sessions (`internal/sessions`, the Claude Code reader). No subsystem reference documents how Claude transcripts are counted, so no page changes.

- Trigger: a `fork-context-ref` line. The reader sets `state.ForkHead` and skips assistant lines until the file's first user line. It does this both in the fast path (`claudeLine`) and in the full parse (`claudeFull`). The first user line clears the flag, and everything after it is counted as before.
- Before: the copied reply counted once in the parent's file and again in each fork's file. After: it counts once, in the parent's file.
- State: `ForkHead` is kept in the parse cache (`fork_head`), so a read that resumes inside the head still skips. `cacheVersion` goes from 22 to 23, so files parsed before are read again.
- Files without a `fork-context-ref` line read as before. These include ordinary subagents, workflow agents and main transcripts.

## Verification

Run at df11f97 (on origin/main 7d075df), go1.27.3 darwin/arm64:

- `gofmt -l` is clean.
- Vet is clean: `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`.
- Builds are ok: `go build`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui` and `GOOS=windows go build`.
- `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...` in a sandbox HOME with Go's caches pinned: 69 packages ok, including `internal/sessions` (ok, 73s). A few packages are red, and they are red in the same way on origin/main 7d075df without this change:
  - `internal/provider`: #3632 (ok in 71s with `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` skipped)
  - `internal/gateway`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `FuzzMarshalRaw` (#3547), `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (#3549), `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (#3680)
  - `internal/plugin`: `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207)
- Broken by hand: I put the old `claude.go` and `sessions.go` back and kept the new test. `TestClaudeForkSubagentCountsParentReplyOnce` then fails with `session: {Input:250 Output:25 CacheRead:30 ...}, want {Input:150 Output:15 CacheRead:20 ...}`. With the change restored, it passes.

issue.title: [Bug] Codex 主动取消请求被计入失败：子代理报告注入时的正常中断拉低成功率

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### 问题

Codex 多代理工作过程中，客户端可能为了接收子代理结果而主动中断正在进行的模型请求。Magpie 将这类请求记录为 `499 / the agent canceled the request`，并计入用量页的失败次数、降低成功率。

建议将「客户端取消」与「上游请求失败」分开统计。正常的代理调度中断不应被直接展示为服务失败。

### 实际观察（已脱敏）

环境：Codex 主代理通过 Magpie 调用 `gpt-6.1-sol`，同时有子代理运行。

下面是一条网关路由记录与本地 Codex 会话事件的对照。时间均改为相对时间，不包含会话 ID、请求 ID、账户身份、本地路径或任务内容：

| 相对时间 | 事件 |
| --- | --- |
| T+0.000s | Magpie 收到主代理的 Sol 请求 |
| T+4.401s | 本地会话记录子代理完成 |
| T+6.239s～T+18.337s | 本地会话记录该 Sol 回复的推理内容；可通过 response ID 与网关请求对应 |
| T+18.344s | 子代理最终报告注入主会话 |
| T+18.346s 左右 | 网关请求结束，记录 `499 / the agent canceled the request`，尝试分类为 `canceled` |
| T+34.531s | 主代理正常继续处理子代理结果，随后完成任务 |

这段上下文没有新的用户消息或用户手动停止事件。子代理报告注入与请求取消相差约 2ms，强烈支持「客户端为纳入子代理结果而中断当前请求」的解释。

证据边界：本地会话没有直接记录 HTTP 请求的内部取消原因，因此上述具体触发原因是基于时序和请求身份对应关系的推断；可以直接确认的是客户端取消、子代理报告同时到达，以及任务随后正常继续。

同一天，我们观察到失败汇总中的 92 次有 91 次属于 `499 / the agent canceled the request`，只有 1 次是最终回复中途断流。这里只逐条核对了上述实例的本地上下文，不能据此断定其余所有取消都来自子代理调度。尽管如此，把取消统一计入失败，会使失败次数和成功率很难反映实际的上游稳定性。

### 预期行为

- 客户端取消作为独立结果展示，仍可在请求列表和详情中追溯。
- 失败次数不把这类主动取消直接当作上游失败；成功率分母也应明确处理取消，避免将取消误算成成功。
- 真正的上游错误、EOF、超时等仍按相应结果统计；已有 Token / 费用记录应保留。

### 简短实现建议

网关已经有 `failCanceled` 分类，并在请求 context 取消且回复尚未结束时设置 499。可以沿用这一分类，为 usage 汇总增加独立的 canceled 结果，而不是让所有 `status >= 400` / error 非空记录统一增加 Errors。

重点检查 `internal/gateway/gateway.go` 的取消处理，以及 `internal/usage/usage.go` 中的 `Failed()`、`Totals.count()` 和成功率计算/失败筛选。若持久化记录没有显式取消类型，可考虑持久化该语义，避免仅凭任意 499 状态码猜测原因。

不建议把所有客户端取消直接改成成功，也不需要把上述具体调度原因当作已被网关证实。

issue.title: Codex app-server is restarted mid-turn: 512 KiB session tail misses task_started, and route includes a catalog magpie doesn't own

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**Version:** v0.1.1845 (05ed578), macOS arm64, official release. The same code is still on main at 4534561f6 (`sessionTurnTail`, and `codexAppRoute` hashing the `model_catalog_json` file).

**What happens.** `KeepCodexAppOnItsProvider` ends the Codex desktop app's own app-server with SIGTERM while a long turn is still running. The app reconnects with `resumedCurrentConversation=false` and the turn stops. Captured with `eslogger signal`: sender `magpie tray`, target the app's bundled `codex` app-server.

**Why the turn counts as idle.** `sessionTurnOpen` (`internal/provider/codex_app_server.go`) reads only the last `sessionTurnTail = 512 << 10` bytes of the rollout. In a long turn the `task_started` record is further back than that and no `task_complete`/`turn_aborted` follows, so `started == ended == -1` and the turn is reported closed. Replaying the rollout up to the signal time: the whole file says a turn is open, the 512 KiB tail says it isn't.

**Why the route changed at all.** Codex's `model_provider` was `openai`, not magpie. `codexAppRoute` (`internal/agent/agents.go`) still hashes the file `model_catalog_json` points to. Here a separate local tool writes that catalog and rewrote it on every Codex models-cache refresh (only `fetched_at` differed), so magpie saw a new route every few minutes and restarted the app-server repeatedly (30+ generations in one day).

**Suggestions.**
1. When the tail has neither marker, read further back (or scan the whole file, or keep a per-file offset of the last lifecycle record) instead of treating it as closed; a file that can't be decided counts as open, as the comment already says for unreadable files.
2. Only include `model_catalog_json`'s content in the route when magpie wrote that catalog or is Codex's provider.
3. Optionally, a setting to turn off the automatic app-server restart.

**Workaround used:** make the third-party catalog writer skip identical rewrites.

issue.title: gateway: a Responses reply to another agent carries events outside the Responses enum (`codex.*`, `response.metadata`, `keepalive`), and a typed client drops the whole turn

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

A turn through a ChatGPT Codex account dies before any of the reply is seen:

```
shell.turn.inference_failed  kind=serialization
serialization error: unknown variant `codex.rate_limits`, expected one of
`response.created`, `response.in_progress`, `response.completed`,
`response.failed`, `response.incomplete`, `response.output_item.added`, ...
```

Grok Build shows it as ``Couldn't read the response: serialization error: unknown variant `codex.rate_limits` … Try sending again.``, magpie's own request log has the turn as `499 the agent canceled the request`, and nothing retries: the client's typed event enum has no name for the event, so the whole turn is lost.

Filtering one such event only uncovers the next behind it: the same turn has since died on `unknown variant \`response.metadata\``, then on `unknown variant \`keepalive\``, and then on `serialization error: missing field \`created_at\``, which is magpie's own `response.failed` ending a stream the upstream cut short.

Seen with magpie 0.1.2284–0.1.2328 and Grok Build 1.0.45–1.0.70 (`xai-grok-sampler`, async-openai's `ResponseStreamEvent`), model `codex/gpt-6.1-terra` asked at `/v1/responses`.

## Repro

The backend's reply keeps the two events it tells only Codex by, and a client that is not Codex is handed them. `POST /v1/responses` with one of the ChatGPT models, as any OpenAI Responses client asks it:

```bash
curl -sS -N -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <magpie key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"codex/gpt-6.1-terra","stream":true,"input":"say OK"}' | grep '^event:'
```

What comes back (the first two lines are the problem):

```
event: codex.rate_limits
event: codex.response.metadata
event: response.created
event: response.in_progress
...
event: response.completed
```

It is intermittent on this route: the same body asked at 00:59 and 01:03 came back with no `codex.*` event at all, and every ask from 01:12 on carried both. `response.metadata` arrives in the middle of a reply, `keepalive` only when the upstream is quiet, and the `response.failed` body appears only when a stream is cut mid-reply — so a client loses some turns and not others, which reads as a flaky upstream rather than a shape problem.

## Why

`passthrough` relays whatever the ChatGPT backend writes. Part of it is the Codex protocol, not the OpenAI Responses API: `codex.rate_limits` and `codex.response.metadata` (the account's windows, the model list's tag), `response.metadata` (the turn's state on a socket, its moderation word on the HTTP route), and a `keepalive` event a quiet upstream sends. A Responses client with a closed event enum — Grok Build's async-openai `ResponseStreamEvent` — reads one of those and ends the turn before the reply: `unknown variant \`codex.rate_limits\``, then `unknown variant \`response.metadata\``, then `unknown variant \`keepalive\``.

The same boundary has a second failure shape. When the upstream stream dies mid-reply, `passthrough` ends it with its own `response.failed` (`streamFailure` in `gateway.go`), which carried only `{"object","status","error"}`. The name is legal, but a typed client reads that `response` into a full `Response` whose `id`, `object`, `created_at`, `model`, `output` and `status` are required, so the turn died on `serialization error: missing field \`created_at\`` — hiding the cut-from-upstream failure behind a parse error, non-retryable.

## Fix

Branch on my fork, rebased on `80ccaba64`: `crayonlu/magpie@codex-lead-events` — https://github.com/crayonlu/magpie/tree/codex-lead-events. PRs here are for collaborators, so the branch rides in this issue.

`internal/gateway/responses_enum.go` holds the OpenAI Responses event enum as a set and a `responsesEnumTidy` that drops every whole SSE frame whose `event:` name (or, where the stream names none, the data's `type`) is not in it. It runs last in `passthrough`'s filter chain, only for `proto == provider.Responses && sse` and only when the client is not Codex — `!fromCodex(r.Header) && agentOf(r) != "codex"`, the pair `codex_own_v1.go` already uses. Codex's own request keeps every event as the backend sent it. The quota tap (`codexLimitsTap`) and failover's `sniff` read the upstream bytes before the filter, so limit accounting and classification are untouched.

`streamFailure` now builds a whole `Response` for `response.failed` (`id`, `object`, `created_at`, `status`, `model`, `output`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `tool_choice`, `tools`, `error`) and carries the stream's next `sequence_number`: `responses_seq.go` watches the last one that went out, so the added event continues the numbering the client reads.

The socket route carries the same guard now: `socketTurnWriter.headerFrames()` returns nothing for a client that isn't Codex, so the `response.metadata` / `codex.response.metadata` / `codex.rate_limits` it synthesizes from the reply's headers no longer reach a foreign typed client on the WebSocket (`responses_ws.go`).

`internal/gateway/responses_enum_test.go` drives the real `/v1/responses` passthrough against a fixture ChatGPT sign-in, one turn with no `User-Agent`, `xai-grok-shell/1.0.45`, `codex_cli_rs/0.166.0`, and `magpie-codex` (a key owned by the codex agent). The first two must get only enum events; the last two must keep `codex.rate_limits`, `codex.response.metadata`, `response.metadata` and `keepalive`. `TestResponsesEnumAllowed` covers the predicate on its own. `TestPassthroughResponsesEndsShort` now asserts the cut-stream `response.failed` carries the full response.

## What was run

macOS arm64, Go 1.27.3, temp `HOME`.

- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -run 'TestResponsesEventsOutsideTheEnumStayWithCodex|TestResponsesEnumAllowed|TestPassthroughResponsesEndsShort' -count=1` — passes at `85e37162e`. With the predicate forced to `true` the same test fails and prints the leaked frames: `event codex.rate_limits there=true`, `event response.metadata there=true`, `event keepalive there=true, want false`. `TestResponsesEnumAllowed` passes under `-race -count=20`.
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -count=1` — 2 reds on this machine, the same 2 on the unpatched tree at `80ccaba64`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `TestMarshalSizedIsJSONMarshal` (#3547, Go 1.27 leaves U+2028/U+2029 unescaped where `encoding/json` does not). No new red.
- `TestResponsesEventsAreClientShaped` walks a translated reply and fails any event without `sequence_number`, or any `response` without `id/object/created_at/status/model/output` — the guard against the next missing field, added after the client reported `missing field sequence_number`.
- `gofmt -l internal/gateway` clean; `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway` and `go build ./...` clean, apart from the darwin cgo deprecation warnings `main` prints.
- Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` at an earlier base of this branch (`4182e68`): 79 packages ok; the only reds were the same gateway environment ones above plus `internal/plugin`'s `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207, Bun 1.4.4 here against a test pinned to 1.4.2).
- Against the running gateway: a build of this branch was installed and driven with `curl`. A non-Codex `User-Agent` got `response.created … response.completed` with none of `codex.*`, `response.metadata` or `keepalive`; `codex_cli_rs` got all of them. The `response.failed` shape was reproduced from a client log (`serialization error: missing field \`created_at\``) and pinned to `streamFailure`.
- `make test-ui` — not run; no GUI file or asset is touched.

issue.title: [Bug] 网关在 key 已报限额用尽后仍先发请求，Gemini 按天额度用完后整天反复被拒（已定位，附修复分支）

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
起因是想让网关在发出请求之前就知道某个 key 已经用不了，而不是先发过去、等几秒拿到 429 再切下一个成员。先核对了两家官方文档，结论是“查询余额”这条路走不通，但有两处可以提前判断的信号 Magpie 目前没有用上。

## 背景：OpenAI / Gemini 的 key 能拿到什么

- **OpenAI**：普通 key 没有余额接口（Usage / Costs API 据社区说法需要 admin key，官方页面 403，未能核实）。响应可以带 `x-ratelimit-limit-*`、`x-ratelimit-remaining-requests|tokens|project-tokens`，以及 `x-ratelimit-reset-*`，后者是一段时长，示例为 `6m0s`、`1s`（[Rate limits 指南](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)：“Responses can include the following header fields”）。限额按模型计，部分模型族共享。
- **Anthropic** 的 API key 带 `anthropic-ratelimit-{requests,tokens,input-tokens,output-tokens}-remaining`，以及 RFC 3339 格式的对应 `-reset`（[Rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits)）。
- **Gemini API**：没有任何接口或响应头报告剩余额度。限额按 project 计（RPM / TPM / RPD），RPD 在太平洋时间午夜重置，只能在 AI Studio 查看用量（[Rate limits](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits)）。

所以能做的“预估”是两件事：OpenAI/Anthropic 用成功响应里的 remaining 头；Gemini 用 429 正文里的 quotaId 推算重置时间。

## Magpie 现在的行为

1. **成功响应里的 remaining 头没人读。** `restAfter` 只在 ≥400 时读 `Retry-After` / `x-ratelimit-reset-*`。一个 key 回 200 且 `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: 0` 时，下一个请求仍然先发给它，吃一个 429 才切换。而且成功路径上的 `hw.header` 只有 `PassedReplyHeaders`（默认只有 request id），即使想在 `servedCandidate` 之后读，也读不到这些头。
2. **Gemini 按天的额度用完后，会整天被反复请求。** Gemini 的 PerDay 429 正文里写着 “Please retry in 33.517s”，RetryInfo 是 `33s`。`resetsAt` 会先读到这个时间，于是 key 只休息约 33 秒（没有这句时则是 `quotaRest` 的 15 分钟）。这个提示说的不是当天额度，额度要到太平洋时间午夜才恢复，所以这个 key 会整天“恢复→被拒→再休息”。`auto/<model>` 组里排在第一的 Gemini key 会让后续每个请求都先失败一次。

## 参考实现

- [分支 `fix/rest-before-rate-limit`](https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/tree/fix/rest-before-rate-limit)
- [提交 3dc7dec6](https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/commit/3dc7dec61fc9a84d75c220b560a385516912721e)
- [对比](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...hhh2210:magpie:fix/rest-before-rate-limit)

改动内容：

- **成功响应带 remaining=0 时提前休息**（`spentRest` / `restIfSpent`，在 `servedCandidate` 之后调用）。OpenAI 的 `x-ratelimit-remaining-*` 或 Anthropic 的 `anthropic-ratelimit-*-remaining` 为 `0`、且对应的 reset 头可以解析时，这个 key 的该模型（`restID`，因为 OpenAI 按模型计；共享限额的模型族要等各自撞到才会休息）休息到 reset，最长 `longestWait`。原始头通过 reply sink 旁路保存（`withLimitSink` → `holdWriter.heardLimits`），不改变转发给 agent 的头；System One 的 decide 路径直接用 `postDecide` 返回的头。只读 OpenAI（api.openai.com）和 Anthropic（api.anthropic.com）官方 API 的各自响应头；中转站转发上游 key 的头时不读，因为那是它某个上游 key 的状态，不代表中转站本身。订阅账号（`Account != nil`）、Anthropic 的 `unified` 头、`LimitRestOff` 的 provider 不受影响。
- **Gemini PerDay 额度休息到太平洋时间午夜**（`geminiDayBackIn`）。仅对 `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` 生效，在 `resetsAt` 之前判断。用户自己设置的 `QuotaResetAt` / `OwnQuotaRest` 仍然优先。其他 host 的同样正文、以及 Gemini PerMinute 额度保持原样。
- `retryAfter` 的三种时间格式解析抽成 `resetIn`，两处共用。
- 同步更新了 `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md` 的两条规则。

生产代码 +166/-9，测试 +190/-0，文档 +2。

## 验证

- `TestSpentLimitRestsBeforeRefusal`（json / stream）：provider 指向 api.openai.com，`s.client` 重定向到 httptest 上游；上游给第一个 key 回 200 + `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Requests: 0` / `X-Ratelimit-Reset-Requests: 6m0s`，经完整 `Server.Handler()` 发两次请求。修复后第二次直接落到另一个 key，并且该 key 的模型休息 6 分钟。把成功路径改回读 `hw.header` 后，测试失败：`asked map[k-spent:2]`。
- `TestSpentRest`：OpenAI 的 requests/tokens（取较长者）、Anthropic 的 RFC 3339 reset、有剩余、无 reset、unified、订阅账号、`LimitRestOff`、中转站、两家的头互相出现在对方 host 上；同时断言休息的 key 是 `restID`。去掉 host 限定后，`relay`、`anthropic's from openai`、`openai's from anthropic` 三项失败。
- `TestGeminiDayQuotaRestsUntilMidnightPacific`：用仓库里已有的真实 PerDay 429 正文（含 33s RetryInfo）。去掉 `geminiDayBackIn`，或把它放在 `resetsAt` 之后（我第一版就是这么写的），测试都会失败：只休息约 33 秒。另外覆盖用户 `QuotaResetAt` 优先、非 Google host 不变、PerMinute 仍按速率限制处理。在 `TZ=UTC`、`Pacific/Kiritimati`、`America/Los_Angeles` 下都跑过。
- `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8`（`go.mod` 的版本）下 `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway` 整包通过（504s）。
- `gofmt -l` 无新增（`internal/library/skillgit_test.go` 在上游原本就有）；macOS、Linux nogui、Windows 的 `go vet ./internal/gateway` 和 `go build ./...` 均通过。
- 完整 `go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`（Go 1.27.3，沙盒 HOME，基于 `03f609e3f`）：78 个包通过。8 个失败用例在干净的 `03f609e3f` 上单独复跑同样失败，且都已有 issue：`TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` / `FuzzMarshalRaw`（#3547，Go 1.27）、`TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`（#3680，Go 1.27）、`TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget`（#3045）、`TestSettingsSaveKeepsWhatItDoesNotSend`（#4514）、`TestPluginSOCKSProxy`（#2207）、`TestNoCommandBypassesProc`（#4491）、`TestColdTurnsTaken`（#4510，`-count=5` 第一轮失败后挂起，和 #4510 中描述的一致）。
- 未做真实使用验收：没有用真实 OpenAI key 观察 remaining 归零，也没有用真实 Gemini key 撞当天额度。

## 未覆盖 / 可以后续做

- askJev 路径（`decide_group.go` 的 `servedCandidate(c, 0)`）拿不到响应头，没有覆盖。embeddings 的 `heardHeaders` sink 没接 limit sink。
- Gemini 没有 remaining 头，所以第一次 429 仍然要实际发出去；改动只是让之后整天不再重复踩。
- 更进一步的“发送前预估”（用 `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` 对比本次请求的 token 估算，不够就跳过）没有做：remaining 只是上一次响应时的快照，并发下会偏乐观，判断阈值需要维护者决定。

了解到仓库不接受外部 PR，所以把问题和参考实现放在这里，供维护者或维护 agent 复现和评估；分支可以直接 cherry-pick，也可以只作参考重新实现。

@yetone 方便时请看一下。

issue.title: [Bug] Claude Desktop 网关模式开了 Enable tool search 后，Copilot 拒绝 tool-search-tool-2025-10-19（400 unsupported beta header），每个会话第一个请求失败，工具搜索实际没生效

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**English summary:** With Claude Desktop's gateway mode pointed at magpie and its *Enable tool search* setting on (`toolSearchEnabled`), Claude Code asks tool search by Bedrock's and Vertex's beta name, `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`, because Desktop runs it with experimental betas off. Copilot's Messages API refuses that name: `400 unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19` on the first request of every Desktop session (and on its `count_tokens` calls). Claude Code then turns tool search off for the session and resends with every tool schema inline, so the setting never takes effect through magpie + Copilot. Copilot serves the same request shape (deferred tools, `tool_reference` results) under Anthropic's own name, `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`, which is what Claude Code sends from a terminal. magpie already renames this beta the other way for Bedrock (`bedrockBetas`). A reference fix renames it for Copilot accounts, with a test and real runs against a Copilot Business account: mdwsk88/magpie, branch [`copilot-tool-search-beta`](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/tree/copilot-tool-search-beta), commit [eed4be36f](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/eed4be36f6c789cddce51eb77c1f9d3ccf08cc64).

## 现象

- 环境：magpie v0.1.1346（macOS app），Claude Desktop 第三方网关模式（自带 Claude Code 2.1.308），模型走 Copilot Business 的 claude-opus-5.5 和 claude-sonnet-5.5。
- 2026-10-24 12:16，在 Desktop 的 Developer › Configure Third-Party Inference 里打开 Enable tool search（magpie 写的那份配置里多了 `toolSearchEnabled: true`）。
- 从那以后，每个新开或恢复的会话，第一个请求都失败。routing 日志记的是 `Copilot: unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`（err_type `invalid_request_body`），当天出现 3 次（12:16、13:15、13:26）。
- Claude Code 收到 400 后不报错，而是关掉这个会话的工具搜索，把所有工具定义内联后重发。以 13:26 那个会话为例：第一个请求 37,411 tokens（其中工具 17,119），重发后 100,290 tokens（工具 71,336），之后每个请求都带着约 10 万 tokens 的工具定义。会话里会出现 "ToolSearch is no longer available" 的提示。
- 所以这个开关经 magpie + Copilot 从来没真正生效过，每个会话还白白多一次失败的请求。

## 原因

- **Claude Code 怎么选 beta 名：** 2.1.308 按实验 beta 是否打开来定。打开时用 Anthropic 自己的名字 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`，关闭时用 Bedrock/Vertex 的名字 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`。
- **Desktop 网关模式发的是哪个：** Desktop 用 `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` 关掉实验 beta。Enable tool search 则通过它传给 CLI 的托管设置 `--managed-settings {"env":{"ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH":"force"}}` 强制打开（CLI 只在 `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1` 时读这份设置）。所以 Desktop 发的是 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`。Desktop 自带的配置说明也写明：网关 provider 只会加这个 beta 值，再加上延迟加载和 `tool_reference`。
- **Copilot 不认这个名字，认另一个：** Copilot 的 `/v1/messages` 和 `count_tokens` 都拒绝 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`，接受 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`。终端里的 Claude Code（自定义 base URL，实验 beta 开着）发的正是这个名字，延迟加载和 `tool_reference` 经 magpie + Copilot 都正常（10-24 实测 13 个请求全部 200）。
- **magpie 只改了一个方向：** `internal/gateway/betas.go` 的 `betas()` 只给 Bedrock 改名（`bedrockBetas`：advanced → tool-search），没有反方向。
- **magpie 也学不会这个拒绝：** `refuseBetas` 只认 Bedrock 的 "Unexpected value(s) … for the `anthropic-beta` header"，认不出 Copilot 的 "unsupported beta header(s): …"，所以每个会话都会再撞一次。就算认出来，去掉这个 beta 后延迟加载也用不了，所以该改名，不该丢掉。

## 修复（参考实现）

mdwsk88/magpie 分支 [`copilot-tool-search-beta`](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/tree/copilot-tool-search-beta)，commit [eed4be36f](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/eed4be36f6c789cddce51eb77c1f9d3ccf08cc64)，基于 upstream 7edf5b0：

- `internal/gateway/betas.go` 新增 `copilotBetas`（`tool-search-tool-2025-10-19` → `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`）。`betas()` 对 Copilot 账号（`p.Account.Agent == "copilot"`）按它改名，改名放在去重之前，所以两个名字一起给时只发一次。`/v1/messages` 和 `count_tokens` 都走 `forward` → `betas()`，两条都覆盖。只改 Copilot；其他 provider 照 Claude Code 给的名字发，Bedrock 的逻辑不变。
- `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`：在讲延迟加载工具的几条后面加了一条说明。
- 新测试 `TestCopilotToolSearchBeta`：
  - 假的 Copilot Messages API 拒绝 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`（错误文本和类型取自 magpie 用量日志里记下的真实拒绝），接受 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`。请求的 beta 列表和形状（`DeferredToolPlaceholder`、延迟的 MCP 工具、`tool_reference`）取自一次真实的 Desktop 网关模式运行。
  - 检查六件事：Copilot 收到改名后的列表，顺序不变，只请求一次；延迟工具和 `tool_reference` 原样到达；终端那个名字原样发出；两个名字无论哪个在前都只发一次；`count_tokens` 也改名，且答案来自 Copilot 而不是 magpie 的估算；不是 Copilot 的 provider 收到原名。

## 验证

在 upstream 7edf5b0 上加这次改动（go1.26.9，macOS，临时 HOME，Go 缓存固定在原位置）：

- **新测试通过。** 故意改坏三种方式，每种都会失败：
  - 去掉改名（即旧代码）：`Desktop's tool search on Copilot: status 400: {"error":{"message":"Copilot: unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19",...}}`。单独测 `count_tokens` 也是同样的 400。
  - 改名对所有 provider 生效：`relay was asked [...advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20...], want ...tool-search-tool-2025-10-19...`。
  - 改名放到去重之后：`Copilot was asked "advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20,advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20"`。
- **构建和全量测试：** 改动的文件 `gofmt -l` 无输出；`go vet ./...` 在 darwin、linux（`-tags nogui`）、windows 上都通过；三个平台的 `go build` 都通过。`go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`：70 个包里 69 个通过（internal/gateway 451 秒）。唯一失败的是 internal/update 的 `TestRelaunchOpenTriedAgain`（`TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat …/003: directory not empty`），和这次改动无关：它在 upstream 7edf5b0 和这个分支上单独各跑 20 次都通过，internal/update 整包在这个分支上 `-count=3` 也通过。从代码看，测试一看到假 `open` 写了 "opened" 就返回，而分离出去的 relaunch shell 还会往那个 TempDir 里的日志追加一条 "open try" 记录（`relaunchScript` 的 `note`），全量测试负载高时会和清理撞上。这个还没单独报。
- **真实验证：** macOS，Copilot Business。临时 HOME 里只放一份 Copilot 登录的副本，`security` 命令换成永远返回"找不到"的替身，所以没有读写真钥匙串，也没有碰正在运行的 magpie 和它的配置。请求方是 Desktop 自带的 Claude Code 2.1.308，带一个 stdio MCP 测试工具，要求模型调用它。

  | magpie | 请求形态 | 结果 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | upstream 7edf5b0 | Desktop 网关模式（`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1`、`CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1`、`--managed-settings {"env":{"ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH":"force"}}`），Sonnet 5.5 | 第一个请求 400 `Copilot: unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`；Claude Code 关掉工具搜索，32 个工具内联重发，请求从 90 KB 变成 149 KB |
  | 修复后 | 同上，Sonnet 5.5；另跑一次 Opus 5.5 [1m] | 全部 200：ToolSearch `select:mcp__probe__echo_probe` → 下一个请求带着 `tool_reference` → 调用延迟加载的 MCP 工具，结果正确；请求一直在约 90 KB |
  | 修复后 | 终端形态（`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`，发 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20` 和其他实验 beta） | 全部 200，同样走通 ToolSearch → `tool_reference` → 调用 |
  | upstream 7edf5b0 / 修复后 | 直接请求 `count_tokens`：Desktop 的 beta 列表加一个延迟工具 | 修复前 400（同一句报错）；修复后 200，`{"input_tokens":77}`，是 Copilot 自己算的数 |

- **没试：** GHE（`*.ghe.com`）上的 Copilot 账号（同一个 `Agent == "copilot"` 分支，没有真账号可试）；修复后的版本接真实 Desktop app（实测用的是同一个 CLI 二进制，参数和环境变量与 Desktop 启动时一致）。

## 用户侧的临时办法

在修复发布前，Enable tool search 配 Copilot 不会生效，每个会话还多一次失败的请求，可以先关掉（同一个菜单，重启 Desktop 后生效）。关掉后上下文用量和现在一样，因为现在本来就在退回全量工具。

## 相关

- #2971 说的是终端里的 Claude Code 对非官方 `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` 默认关闭工具搜索，开关是 `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`；这里是 Desktop 网关模式，开关是 Desktop 的 `toolSearchEnabled`，问题出在 beta 的名字上。
- 没改：`refuseBetas` 认不出 Copilot 的拒绝措辞（`unsupported beta header(s): x`），所以 Copilot 拒绝的其他 beta 也不会被记住和去掉，每次都会失败。这次的 beta 不能靠去掉解决，所以没放进这个修复；需要的话可以另开一个。

issue.title: gateway: let progressing uploads outlast the routing hold (#4775)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
A large request uploaded over a slow connection can exhaust the unrouted watchdog before Magpie reads the model. On latest main `9d08993c8bd40de5d002bc364a16be344c5d78fa`, this already returns a body-specific 408 rather than the older 504 reported in yetone/magpie#4775, but retrying the same upload still hits the two-minute cutoff.

This change credits time spent reading the body at one second per 32 KiB actually received on the wire. Credit is capped at actual body-read time, so it cannot extend a subsequent internal hold. The 32 KiB/s threshold leaves room below the report's measured 44–53 KB/s without allowing a byte-at-a-time client to hold the gateway indefinitely. The two-minute base allowance, 30-second unknown-work watchdog, 60-second wire-idle deadline, body-room queue and decoded size cap remain. Upload allowance failures remain 408 with received-byte diagnostics, now suggesting checking the connection/proxy or compacting the conversation and reducing inline images before retrying.

Implementation: `internal/gateway/unrouted.go`, reusing `bodyRead` and the existing body wait accounting. Contract: `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`. No new per-read timers or goroutines.

Regression coverage goes through the real `Front()` stack over TLS to a local fake provider: declared-length, chunked, gzip and zstd uploads outlast the routing budget, reach no provider until complete, and are forwarded exactly once. Additional tests cover the rate boundary, fast uploads not banking time for later internal holds, and the idle deadline despite earned credit. Existing trickle, body-room, masking and unknown-work tests remain relevant.

Reviewed head: `f689e404` (upload fix), on prerequisite `acb2249e` and upstream main `9d08993c`. Validation on macOS arm64, Go 1.26.8 and Bun 1.4.3:

- Initial regression against unchanged main: `TestUnroutedProgressingUploadOutlastsMost` FAIL, HTTP 408 after the scaled one-second routing budget.
- Restoring main's budget calculation via Go overlay with the final tests: all four TLS upload cases FAIL with 408; the budget-boundary test also FAILS. No compile-error-only claim.
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -run 'TestUnrouted|TestRequestBody|TestMaskingModelWaitNotCutOffAtMost' -count=1`: PASS, 28.267s.
- The same selection with `-race -count=20`: PASS, 547.523s.
- Changed-file gofmt and `git diff --check`: clean. Native, Linux (`nogui`) and Windows `go vet ./...`: PASS. All three builds: PASS.
- First full suite: gateway PASS, 743.006s; 85 packages passed, with failures in claudebridge and plugin. `TestCallbackGoesPastTheAgentsProxy` timed out waiting for its helper; its isolated `-race -count=20` passed (3.586s). The unresolved failure and diagnostic gap are tracked in https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/4782; it is not claimed fixed.
- `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` was the known Bun 1.4.3 assertion mismatch in #2207. This branch first takes skygunner's existing `a93c613a02a376e559f0884ad8cf1b865681927d` unchanged as `acb2249e`, retaining its author, to unblock the suite. The plugin regression passes `-race -count=20`; all three vets pass again. This is a separate prerequisite test-only commit.
- Final `go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`: PASS, exit 0, 87 packages (32 cached), 18 packages with no test files, 1152.1s wall time. Gateway ran again: 734.881s; plugin: 122.229s; claudebridge: 3.813s. The first-run callback failure remains tracked in #4782 despite this pass. Non-verbose suite output does not enumerate individual skipped tests; no skip count is claimed.

The compiler reports existing macOS deprecated-API and enum-conversion warnings. LSP found no new errors; it reported existing map-copy hints and a masking lock warning outside the changed logic, with incomplete clean-file coverage.

Scope: the original conversation and live gateways were not touched. This reproduces the watchdog interaction locally; it does not establish the cause of the original network throughput or claim a live Linux end-to-end verification. No UI assets changed. All test providers are local fixtures and Go runs use a temporary HOME with pinned GOPATH/GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE.

This PR is hosted on the reporter's fork for review because upstream's API reports `pullRequestCreationPolicy: COLLABORATORS_ONLY` and this account has READ permission. Related upstream issue: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/4775 .

issue.title: gateway: slow request-body uploads hit pre-routing 504 with misleading retry/restart guidance (0.1.1255)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

A long Pi conversation repeatedly received `504: magpie held this request for 2m0s without routing it to any provider` through a Remote Magpie connection. The remote gateway's watchdog dump showed handlers waiting for TLS request-body bytes in `readSized`, before provider selection. Switching from an automatic routing group to an explicit Codex route produced the same failure.

Compacting the conversation and restoring the original automatic route recovered the session: a bounded probe returned `ROUTE_OK` in approximately 7 seconds. The error's recommendation to resend or restart Magpie was misleading for this case; resending the same large context repeatedly encountered the same upload bottleneck.

## Environment and scope

- Client: Pi running on macOS, through a local Magpie gateway.
- Transport: local Magpie → remote Magpie over HTTPS on a slow international/private-network connection.
- Remote gateway: **0.1.1255**, Linux, running as a user service. The serving executable path was checked, rather than relying on a potentially different CLI on PATH.
- Endpoints seen in the remote logs: `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`.
- The automatic group used `routing=smart`, `stays=auto`, with Codex and TRAE members serving the same GPT model.
- **Not reproduced on the current latest release.** At filing time GitHub reports `v0.1.2597`. This report describes the deployed version above; it does not establish that the behavior remains in the latest version.

## Observed behavior

The client repeatedly received:

```text
Singapore Magpie: magpie held this request for 2m0s without routing it to any provider,
so it was stopped rather than left waiting. Send it again; if it keeps happening,
restart magpie and report it with magpie's log, which says where it was held.
(504: you can retry your request)
```

A representative server log was:

```text
gateway: POST /v1/responses for ? from pi held 2m0s before routing,
not masking it; stopped with 504; where every goroutine stood:
```

Relevant frames from the watchdog dump (unrelated goroutines omitted):

```text

```

## Checks and recovery

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Small fresh requests through the automatic group and explicit Codex route | Both returned HTTP 200 in approximately 4 seconds |
| Original long conversation switched to explicit Codex route | Same remote pre-routing 504 |
| Independent synthetic 1 MB request uploaded directly to the remote HTTPS gateway | 1,000,090 bytes uploaded in 18.72 seconds, approximately 53 KB/s; received the expected unknown-model 404 after body parsing |
| Synthetic 20 MB request uploaded directly to the remote HTTPS gateway, with a 40-second client cutoff | Only 1,769,472 bytes uploaded in 40 seconds, approximately 44 KB/s; curl timed out (the measurement ran alongside a local-forwarding probe) |
| Two native Pi compactions, then restore the original automatic group | Same conversation returned `ROUTE_OK` in approximately 7 seconds; normal completion, no tool calls |

The retained transcript suffix was approximately 23.4 MB before recovery, including substantial image data, and approximately 5.3 MB after the two compactions. **These are serialized transcript measurements, not captured HTTP Content-Length values.** Raw history remained intact; compaction appended checkpoints and reduced the context sent on subsequent turns.

The evidence supports a request-body transfer bottleneck preceding routing. The underlying reason for the low network throughput is not established, and the dump alone does not distinguish continuous slow progress from pauses between reads. No routing-group policy change or shared gateway restart was needed to recover this conversation.

## Suggested reproduction

This is a synthetic reproducer for maintainers to try; the exact throttled command below has **not** been run as a full end-to-end reproduction. The measurements above used the naturally slow connection.

1. Run an HTTPS Magpie gateway with a gateway key.
2. Generate a large JSON body. An intentionally unknown model avoids an upstream inference call while still exercising body parsing:

   ```bash
   python3 - <<'PY'
   import json
   with open('/tmp/magpie-slow-body.json', 'w') as f:
       json.dump({
           'model': 'route-diagnostic-invalid-model',
           'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'x' * 20_000_000}],
       }, f)
   PY
   ```

3. Upload it at a controlled slow rate, using a gateway URL and key supplied through environment variables:

   ```bash
   curl --silent --show-error \
     --limit-rate 50k --max-time 180 \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAGPIE_GATEWAY_KEY" \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data-binary @/tmp/magpie-slow-body.json \
     "$MAGPIE_BASE_URL/chat/completions" \
     -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code} uploaded=%{size_upload} seconds=%{time_total}\n'
   ```

4. Inspect whether the unrouted watchdog aborts the upload around two minutes, which read stage it reports, and whether a progressing upload is distinguished from an idle or stalled body.

## Expected behavior / possible improvements

- Distinguish request-body upload waits from provider-selection waits in the client-facing error and diagnostic report.
- Report bytes received / expected, elapsed upload time, and last-progress age where available. This would make the reason actionable without interpreting a full goroutine dump.
- If an absolute upload limit intentionally terminates the request, explain that limit and suggest reducing/compacting the request or checking the connection. Resending unchanged data or restarting the gateway should not be the primary guidance for this condition.
- Check that the body idle timeout and the unrouted watchdog interact as intended for uploads that continue making progress. A regression test could cover a progressing upload that outlasts the unrouted budget, while retaining protection against genuinely stalled clients.

## Related reports

- #4602: similar client-facing pre-routing 504 wording; this report adds body-read stacks and transfer measurements.
- #2567 and #4511: request-body progress / timeout classification tests.
- #4766: a long Pi session also fails before routing, but its reported bottleneck is masking after the body has been read. The observed wait here is in TLS/body reads.

No conversation contents, images, credentials, internal addresses, or full diagnostic dumps are included.

issue.title: [Bug] 走 Messages API 的 Claude 回复，用量里的推理 token 恒为 0（aUsage 不读 output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens）

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**English summary:** magpie's usage records how much of a reply was reasoning for Chat (`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`), Responses and Gemini (`thoughtsTokenCount`) replies, and for the Claude subscription path (`cliUsage.gateway()` reads `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`). The Anthropic Messages path doesn't: `aUsage` in `internal/gateway/anthropic.go` has no `output_tokens_details`, so every Claude reply over the Messages API (Anthropic, Copilot, Bedrock, relays) is recorded with reasoning 0, whether it is relayed (`usageSniffer`) or translated (the Anthropic decoder). As a result `reasoning_tokens` is 0 in `magpie usage --csv` for all of that traffic, `DecodeOf` times such a reply as if it had no reasoning, and a Chat/Responses upstream's reasoning count is dropped when its reply is translated for an Anthropic client such as Claude Code (the Chat and Responses encoders do carry it). A reference fix with tests is on mdwsk88/magpie, branch `gateway-anthropic-thinking-tokens` (commit [9feac29c6](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/9feac29c6c5f1bd7e0601dc9c77be0bbfb0f4395)).

## 现象

Claude Code（Claude Desktop 的第三方模式）经 magpie 用 Copilot 的 claude-opus-5.5。Copilot 每个回复的 `message_delta` 都带思考 token 数，例如 2026-10-24 的一次（effort high）：

```
"usage":{"cache_creation_input_tokens":3858,"cache_read_input_tokens":12030,"input_tokens":2,...,"output_tokens":1277,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":710}}
```

magpie 记下的这一行：output 1277，reasoning 0。2026-10-23 我们做 A/B 测试时，magpie 记下的 277 个经 Copilot 的 claude-desktop 请求，`magpie usage --csv` 的 `reasoning_tokens` 每一行都是 0；同一批运行里，Claude Code 自己的 result 用量都带思考 token 数。

## 原因

- `internal/gateway/anthropic.go` 的 `aUsage` 只读 input、output、cache 几个字段，没有 `output_tokens_details`，`aUsage.usage()` 也就不会填 `Usage.Reasoning`。
- 透传的回复（`sniff.go` 的 Anthropic 分支）和转译的回复（Anthropic 解码器处理 `message_delta`）都经过它，所以两条路都丢。
- 同一个仓库里，`claude_subscription.go` 的 `cliUsage.gateway()` 读了 `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`；Chat、Responses、Gemini 的用量也都填了 `Reasoning`。只有 Messages API 这一处漏了。
- 和 #1578 不是同一个原因：那里是请求被路由到 Chat Completions 才丢了思考统计，这里是 Messages API 本身的用量没读这个字段。
- 反方向同理：`Usage.anthropic()` 不写思考 token，Chat 或 Responses 上游的推理数转给 Claude Code 时被丢掉；`Usage.chat()` 和 Responses 的编码都带着。

## 影响

- 用量页和 CSV 里，所有走 Messages API 的 Claude 请求推理数都是 0（Anthropic 官方 API、Copilot、Bedrock、各种中转）。
- 输出速度：`DecodeOf` 对有推理数的回复，只按回答部分、从第一个文字算起；Claude 回复的推理数是 0，就按整段输出（含思考）、从第一个内容算起，和其他协议的口径不一致。
- Claude Code 接 Chat 或 Responses 上游时，拿不到思考 token 数。

## 修复（参考实现）

mdwsk88/magpie 分支 `gateway-anthropic-thinking-tokens`，commit [9feac29c6](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/9feac29c6c5f1bd7e0601dc9c77be0bbfb0f4395)：

- `aUsage` 加 `OutputTokensDetails{ThinkingTokens}`，`usage()` 把它填进 `Usage.Reasoning`；
- `Usage.anthropic()` 在 `Reasoning > 0` 时写回 `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`（为 0 时输出不变）。

新测试：

- `TestAnthropicThinkingTokensCounted`：用上面那次 Copilot 回复的原始字节（签名截短），分别经 `/v1/messages`、`/v1/chat/completions`、`/v1/responses`，检查用量行的 reasoning 是 710，以及客户端拿到的 usage 里有这个数。
- `TestTranslatedReasoningToldAsThinkingTokens`：Chat 上游报 `reasoning_tokens: 100`，Claude Code 客户端的 `message_delta` 里应有 `"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":100}`。

## 验证

在 upstream b437e4a 上加这次改动（go1.26.9，macOS，临时 HOME，Go 缓存固定在原位置）：

- 两个新测试通过。把 `anthropic.go` 换回原样后两个都失败：三条路径都报 `thinking tokens not counted: 200 output 1277 reasoning 0`；转译的回复报 `message_delta doesn't tell the thinking tokens`。
- 改动的文件 `gofmt -l` 无输出；`go vet ./...` 在 darwin、linux（`-tags nogui`）、windows 上都通过；三个平台 `go build` 都通过。
- `go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`：69 个包全部通过（internal/gateway 426 秒）。
- 没试：拿改过的版本接真实上游。测试用的是 Copilot 真实回复的字节；Anthropic 官方 API 也返回同一个字段。

## 相关观察（不在这次修复里）

- Copilot 的 `message_delta` 还带 `copilot_usage`：按类型列出 token 数和单价，以及 `total_nano_aiu`（上面那次是 4724400000）。magpie 的 credits 字段现在只给 WorkBuddy 的 `usage.credit` 用；如果想显示 Copilot 的 AI 用量，可以从这里取。
- 顺带确认过、不需要改 magpie 的两件事：
  - Copilot 单次回复超过约 630 秒会被对端断开（`CANCEL; received from peer`），magpie 已经按协议补发 `event: error`（`streamFailure`）。
  - Copilot 不发思考进度（`thinking_delta` 里没有 `estimated_tokens`）。magpie 转发了 `thinking-token-count-2026-05-13` beta，是 Copilot 那边没给。

issue.title: [Bug] Copilot 的 Claude 1 小时缓存写入按 5 分钟价计费，magpie 按 2× 输入记账（OneHourFor），Tune 的缓存建议也按 Anthropic 价算

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**English summary:** Copilot bills Claude's 1-hour cache writes at its 5-minute write price (claude-opus-5.5: $5 per 1M, 1.25× input), as its own `copilot_usage` on every reply shows. magpie fills in a Claude model's missing 1-hour price as Anthropic's 2× input for every provider (`catalog.OneHourFor`), so `copilot/claude-opus-5.5` is priced at $8 per 1M for 1-hour writes. On three real requests, magpie's recorded cost matches Copilot's own figure to the micro-dollar for a 5-minute write and for a cache read, and is 60% higher for a 1-hour write ($0.125456 vs $0.078443). Tune's cache-TTL advice makes the same assumption in its own weights (`tune.WeightsFor`: any `claude*` model at read 0.1, write 1.25, 1-hour write 2), whatever provider served the calls. At Copilot's rates (read 0.05, write = 1-hour write = 1.25) a 1-hour cache never costs more than a 5-minute one. This is the class LESSONS.md calls "scope a vendor rule to that vendor" (71d2da1f priced Anthropic's 1-hour write onto OpenAI models).

## 现象

2026-10-24，Claude Code（CLI 2.1.308）经 magpie 0.1.1346 调 `copilot/claude-opus-5.5`。对比同一个请求的两份费用：magpie 记的（`magpie usage --csv` 的 `cost_usd`），以及 Copilot 在 `message_delta` 里自己报的（`copilot_usage.total_nano_aiu`，按 1 AIU = $0.01 换算）。表里前两行完全一致，说明这个换算没错。

| 请求 | 用量 | Copilot 报的费用 | magpie 记的费用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 写 5 分钟缓存 | input 2、output 4、读 12,338、写 3,458（5 分钟） | $0.019846 | $0.019846 |
| 只读缓存 | input 2、output 4、读 15,671 | $0.003222 | $0.003222 |
| 写 1 小时缓存 | input 2、output 4、写 15,671（1 小时） | $0.078443 | **$0.125456** |

- 第三个请求在 Copilot 的 `copilot_usage.token_details` 里是 `cache_write` 15,671 个，`cost_per_batch` 500,000,000,000（每 1,000,000 个），也就是 $5/M，和 5 分钟写入同价；加上输入、输出，正好等于它报的 `total_nano_aiu` 7,844,300,000。
- `magpie model price copilot/claude-opus-5.5` 显示 cache write $5 (5 min)、$8 (1 hour)。其余各项（$4 输入、$20 输出、$0.2 读、$5 写）都和 Copilot 的一致，只有 1 小时写入不同。
- 实际会话的量级：一个长会话设了 `promptCacheTtl: "1h"` 后的第一个请求，往 1 小时档写了 465,864 token。magpie 记 $3.74，按 Copilot 的价格是 $2.35。

## 原因

1. **费用。** `internal/catalog/catalog.go` 的 `OneHourFor`：模型 id 含 `claude`、有 5 分钟写入价、没有 1 小时价时，一律填 `CacheWrite1h = 2 * Input`，理由是 Anthropic 对所有模型都这么收。它在 `provider.priceOf`（`models.go`）、sessions、CLI 和 catalog 里被调用，都不看提供方。Copilot 给的价格没有 1 小时这一项，于是被套上了 Anthropic 的 2 倍。
2. **Tune 的缓存建议。** `internal/tune/tune.go` 的 `WeightsFor` 只按模型名前缀给权重：`claude*` 是读 0.1、写 1.25、1 小时写 2；其他是读 0.1、写 1、1 小时写 1。`CacheTTL` 用第一条调用的模型（`WeightsFor(cs[0].Model)`）给所有调用定价，不看提供方，也不读 magpie 自己的价表。
   - 按 Anthropic 的权重，1 小时写入比 5 分钟贵 60%，只有足够多的调用落在上一条之后 5–60 分钟内，Tune 才会建议 1 小时。
   - 按 Copilot 的价格，1 小时写入和 5 分钟同价，延长缓存只会把一部分重写变成读，所以在任何调用序列上 `replayTTL` 算出的 1 小时总价都不高于 5 分钟。
   - 用哪套权重取决于 agent 运行时用的模型名，和实际由谁服务无关。

## 影响

- 用量页和 CSV 的费用：经 Copilot、用 1 小时缓存的 Claude 请求，写缓存这一项多算 60%。长会话第一次写 1 小时缓存时，这个差额很明显（上面那次多算 $1.40）。
- Tune 的缓存建议：经 Copilot 的调用会按 Anthropic 的价格比较，1 小时档的成本被高估，可能建议保持 5 分钟，而在 Copilot 上 1 小时档从不更贵。

## 建议（未实现，供参考）

- `OneHourFor` 只用在确实按 2 倍收 1 小时写入的提供方（我们只核对了 Anthropic 官方价和 Copilot）。Copilot 的 Claude 1 小时写入按它的 5 分钟价算；也可以直接记 Copilot 每个回复自带的 `copilot_usage.total_nano_aiu`，它和 magpie 现有算法在其他各项上分毫不差。
- Tune 用服务这些调用的提供方的实际价格回放（比如 `provider.EffectivePriceIn`），而不是按模型名套 Anthropic 的价格。

## 相关观察

Tune 只回放 `claude`（命令行）和 `codex` 两个 agent 的调用（`internal/gui/tune.go` 的 `tuneOf`），Claude Desktop 的 Code 标签页（`claude-desktop`）不在里面。但 Tune 写的 `promptCacheTtl`（`~/.claude/settings.json`）对 Desktop 的 Code 标签页同样生效：加上 `"promptCacheTtl": "1h"` 后，正在运行的 Desktop Code 会话的下一个请求就按 1 小时档写入了 465,864 token，再下一个全部读缓存（2026-10-24 08:25 的 magpie 用量记录）。如果把 `claude-desktop` 也纳入，Desktop 的用户也能拿到这条建议。

## 怎么测的

Claude Code 2.1.308（Claude Desktop 自带），`-p`、effort low、提示"只回复 OK"，经 magpie 0.1.1346 调 `copilot/claude-opus-5.5`。表里第一行是默认 5 分钟缓存的请求；第三行是设了 `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` 的请求；第二行是第三行 7.5 分钟后用同样前缀再发的一次（全部读缓存，说明 1 小时档确实生效）。`copilot_usage` 取自 Claude Code 输出的原始事件流，费用取自 `magpie usage --csv`。

issue.title: [feat] 联网搜索：可选的并行多源搜索，去重合并全部结果（附 80 题实测）

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**English summary:** magpie asks its search APIs in order and returns the first one that answers (`apiSearch` in `internal/gateway/search_api.go`). On an 80-query benchmark in Chinese and English, with answers registered before running, no single API was best on both query sets. Merging the deduplicated results of several APIs scored significantly higher than the best single API, with no query lost (60-query set: 108 → 114–117 of 120, sign test p ≤ 0.03), at 1.7–2.4× the returned text. Interleaving down to the same 6 results gained only 1–3 points (not significant), and routing by query language didn't help. Proposal: an opt-in mode that asks the selected APIs in parallel and returns their deduplicated union, capped. Related: #2286 (a comment there by @moon16u proposes the same idea).

## 背景

现在的联网搜索按列表顺序逐家问搜索 API，第一家有结果就返回，不并行、不合并（`internal/gateway/search_api.go` 的 `apiSearch`）。Claude Code 的 WebSearch、Codex 的 web_search 和 web-search MCP 三个入口都经过它。#2286 下 @moon16u 提过"并行多源搜索"；这里补充实测数据，说明哪种合并方式真正有用。

## 测试方法

- 两组题共 80 题：第一组 20 题，第二组 60 题（中文 28、英文 32）。覆盖英文技术文档、中文平台文档（微信、钉钉、飞书、鸿蒙等）、中英文报错排查、云服务限制、大模型 API、百科常识、近期资讯。
- 每题在跑之前登记官方来源域名和标准答案（正则）。第二组每题的答案都不在查询词里，由脚本核对。
- 三家搜索 API：You.com（免 key）、Tavily、DeepSeek（`/v1/tools/search`）。通过 magpie 的 `/mcp/magpie/web-search` 逐家测：每次用 `magpie search off/on` 只开一家。magpie 0.1.1285，macOS。
- 用三家的原始结果离线模拟合并方案：交替（round-robin）取前 6 或前 8、RRF 取前 6、去重后全部，以及按查询语言分流。每个方案逐题与最好的单家配对比较，做符号检验。
- 评分：前 N 条里有没有登记的官方站点（权威来源），返回文字里有没有标准答案（答案）。每题满分 2。得分有变化的题已逐条人工核对。

## 结果（第二组 60 题，满分 120）

| 方案 | 权威来源 | 答案 | 合计 | 返回篇幅 | 对比最好单家 胜/负 | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 只用 You.com（这组最好） | 52 | 56 | 108 | 1.0× | — | — |
| 只用 Tavily | 52 | 49 | 101 | 1.1× | | |
| 只用 DeepSeek | 38 | 56 | 94 | 0.7× | | |
| You.com + DeepSeek 交替前 6 | 53 | 58 | 111 | 0.9× | 6/3 | 0.51 |
| You.com + Tavily 交替前 6 | 54 | 56 | 110 | 1.1× | 5/3 | 0.73 |
| 三家交替前 8 | 56 | 58 | 114 | 1.3× | 8/2 | 0.11 |
| You.com + DeepSeek 去重全部 | 55 | 59 | 114 | 1.7× | 6/0 | 0.03 |
| You.com + Tavily 去重全部 | 58 | 57 | 115 | 1.8× | 7/0 | 0.02 |
| 三家去重全部 | 58 | 59 | 117 | 2.4× | 9/0 | 0.004 |
| 按语言分流（中文走 DeepSeek 或 You.com） | 49–52 | 54–57 | 104–106 | 1.0× | 不优于最好单家 | ≥0.45 |

第一组 20 题的结论一致：最好的单家（这组是 Tavily）得 25/27，去重合并得 27/27，一题不输。不过题太少，算不出显著性。

## 结论

1. 没有一家总是最好：第一组 Tavily 最好，第二组 You.com 最好。DeepSeek 的答案命中高（56/60），但来自官方站点的少（38/60）。
2. 只取 6 条交替合并，只多 1–3 分，不显著。新挤进来的好结果会挤掉原有的好结果，例如 man7.org 的 tcp(7)、Moonshot 的官方文档被挤了出去。
3. 去重后合并全部结果显著提分，一题不输。代价是返回篇幅变成 1.7–2.4 倍、每次搜索消耗每一家的额度、延迟取最慢的一家（实测中位 1.1–1.5 秒）。
4. 按语言分流没有帮助。

## 建议（默认关闭）

- 增加可选的"并行合并"模式：用户勾选 2 到 N 个已启用的搜索源，例如 `magpie search mix you,tavily` 和 `magpie search mix off`，设置页的搜索列表里也放一个开关。
- 在该模式下，`apiSearch` 并行调用选中的源，各自沿用 `askSearchAPIKeys` 的超时、换 key 和休息逻辑。结果按规范化后的 URL 去重，按名次交替排列，截到总条数上限（建议默认 10–12 条，可设置），每条标注来源。
- 某一家失败、超时或没有结果，不影响其他家；全部失败时按现在的顺序回退。

issue.title: Gemini AI Studio keys missing from search-provider selection — fork fix ready for pickup/review

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
The native Gemini API work from #4935 works with my real AI Studio key, but Google Gemini still appears under “cannot be selected as a search provider” in Settings → Web search on v0.1.2767.

Fix: [li-yifei/magpie, fix/gemini-key-searcher](https://github.com/li-yifei/magpie/tree/fix/gemini-key-searcher), commit [45aa2c3f9e676cb062c2be2bce5a567b63704f30](https://github.com/li-yifei/magpie/commit/45aa2c3f9e676cb062c2be2bce5a567b63704f30), based on upstream `8e9b048b65ff8630e1f11c57783c4808861d7a12`. Three files: the eligibility fix, regression tests, and the gateway design reference.

With the official Chat endpoint and native Gemini endpoint configured, a direct search on `google/models/gemini-3.8-flash` already returns a completed search and Google grounding sources. The remaining failure is selecting this provider to search for other models.

### Reproduction

1. Configure Google Gemini with an AI Studio API key and `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta` as its native Gemini endpoint.
2. Enable a searchable Gemini model.
3. Open Settings → Web search → Search provider.

Expected: Google Gemini is selectable, and automatic selection can use it when higher-ranked search providers are unavailable.

Observed: it is excluded from the picker, and an explicitly stored selection is rejected as incapable of searching.

### Cause and scope

`geminiKeySearches` already supports native requests, own-provider search, model filtering and readiness. `searchRank` only includes Google sign-ins, so both the manual picker and automatic selection exclude AI Studio keys.

The fork patch adds AI Studio keys to the existing Google search rank and exposes the existing own-provider preference through `SearcherChoice.Own`. It uses the existing native request path and Google endpoint checks. Cleared native endpoints, unrelated hosts, Vertex AI and non-searchable models retain their existing restrictions.

This is a small follow-up to the built-in provider implementation. It introduces no plugin, configuration inheritance, dependency, credential storage change, workflow or release change.

### Verification

- Removed both changed eligibility expressions: all three new regression tests failed. The picker returned `[]`, the AI Studio rank was `-1`, and another provider's search failed with “no provider that can search the web, nor a search API, is set up in magpie”.
- Restored the fix: the three new tests and four existing AI Studio/native-search tests passed. The new regressions also passed with `-race`.
- `gofmt -l` and `git diff --check` were clean. Native, Linux/nogui and Windows vet and builds passed. Tests used a temporary HOME with the existing Go caches pinned.
- Real-key check on macOS: ran the patched binary on separate loopback ports with a temporary configuration containing the existing AI Studio key. The actual GUI `/api/settings` response included Google Gemini in `searchChoices`, with `own: true`, and showed it as both the named and automatic search provider. An MCP `web_search` through the patched gateway using `google/models/gemini-3.8-flash` succeeded and returned Google grounding redirect sources. The installed app, executable and user configuration were preserved.

Two full `go test -tags nogui ./...` runs, including the final tree with the new tests, failed in the same three existing tests (Go 1.26.8, macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.4):

- `TestCodexPoolSaysTheClientsVersion`: the same `0.165.0` versus `0.161.0` mismatch documented in #4807. It passed when run alone at the clean base.
- `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`: HTTPS CONNECT returned a `proxyconnect tcp: 502 Bad Gateway: socks connect ...` error, matching #2207 and its comments. The same failure reproduced at the clean base.
- `TestLaneLimitRoutes`: `/api/lanes` returned an active lane where the test expected `{}`. It passed alone at the clean base; I have not established the full-suite trigger or found an exact existing issue.

These failures are disclosed for review; the unrelated tests are unchanged. Cross-platform vet/builds do not establish Linux or Windows runtime behavior. No GUI asset changed, and the Chromium/WebKit UI suites were not run; the GUI verification above exercised the real settings API.

Following `docs/contributors.md`, I am submitting the fix through an issue and a branch on my fork. Please have the maintainer/review bot pick up the linked commit, review it and run the required checks on the merge result.

issue.title: provider: opt-in GLM API-key auto-reset on quota exhaustion (scoped patch + live API evidence)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
This delivers a small, provider-key-only auto-reset patch for #2568 and #2716, with a fresh live check of BigModel's API-key authentication. Thanks to @Jichao for the endpoint investigation in #2716; the commit credits that contribution.

### Live evidence (2026-11-05)

Using the personal GLM Coding Plan API key already configured in Magpie, without a ZCode or browser session:

- `GET https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/biz/customer-package-reset/list?targetType=PERSONAL` returned available weekly cards.
- `POST /api/biz/customer-package-reset/use`, with the bare API key in `Authorization` and `{targetType: "PERSONAL", resetType: "WEEK", recordId: <selected ID>, grantType: "GLOBAL", requestId: <UUID>}`, returned `code: 200, success: true`.
- A separate quota read changed five-hour usage **100% → 0%** and weekly usage **69% → 0%**. Available weekly cards changed **3 → 2**.

This was an explicitly authorized manual API call. It verifies the vendor protocol and weekly-card behavior; it is not a live test of the new automatic gateway path. No account IDs, keys or sessions are included here. Z.ai has not been live-tested by this contribution.

### Proposed behavior and patch scope

`magpie provider auto-reset <id> on|off` opts one personal GLM plan key into automatic consumption. Default: off. It follows the exact key and vendor; replacing a key does not inherit consent. The initial command enables single-key providers; disabling remains possible after adding another key.

After every candidate is unavailable and a request receives a quota-exhaustion refusal, the gateway re-reads personal quota, chooses the matching unexpired card with the earliest expiry, consumes it, verifies quota recovery and retries the request. Weekly exhaustion takes priority. A five-hour exhaustion does not automatically spend a more valuable weekly card if no five-hour card exists.

A separate per-key, machine-local state file and cross-process lock protect consumption. The original window deadline, selected record and request ID are written atomically **before** the POST. Uncertain responses, failed writes/reads/locks and restarts cannot turn into another automatic POST during that window. Toggling off/on preserves the reservation. Codex's state and history remain separate.

This patch covers API-key providers. ZCode plugin accounts, team cards, expiry scheduling, peak-hour policy and a GUI settings switch are outside this first patch. The routing story identifies GLM in all supported translations. Automated consumption should be enabled on only one machine for a given key.

### Delivery and verification

Draft PR on my fork: https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/pull/2

Commit: https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/commit/8ab06857d82695bcdb077ace24b558a74c7519f2

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie.git feat/glm-key-auto-reset
git cherry-pick 8ab06857d82695bcdb077ace24b558a74c7519f2
```

Based on upstream `435f04151`. Diff: production **+266/-2**, tests **+288/-0**, docs **+39/-0**.

Passed:
- Focused provider, CLI and gateway tests; provider/gateway `-race -count=3` (sandbox HOME/config, pinned Go caches).
- Behavioral regression: disabling the new gateway integration makes `TestGLMAutoResetRequest` fail with HTTP 429 / zero spends / one attempt; restoring it gives HTTP 200 / one spend / successful retry.
- Native, Linux and Windows vet/build; built CLI on/off under synthetic configuration; formatting/diff checks.
- Headless Chromium routing-story checks in English and Chinese, including GLM text. Full provider and CLI packages pass.

Not green / not run:
- Full `go test -tags nogui ./...`: JSON marshal parity failures (#5348, reproduced on unchanged base), gateway package exceeded its 10-minute budget, `TestLaneLimitRoutes` (#5150), `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207; existing fix branch is tracked there).
- `i18n-keys`: existing #5332 failure (`View routing` in a Go-test comment).
- WebKit, full browser suite and live automatic spending not run. Environment: macOS arm64, Go 1.27.3, Bun 1.4.4.

No production Magpie binary or auto-reset setting was changed.

The live automatic-spend gate requested in #2716 remains open. Please treat this as a **draft for review**, not a claim that all merge gates passed. A real card was already used for the protocol check; no further cards were spent just to generate test evidence.

For integration, please cherry-pick the linked commit with its author retained. If squashing or reimplementing the patch, please preserve `Co-authored-by: hhh2210 <hzy2210@gmail.com>` and the contribution credit already in the commit.

issue.title: plugin tests: TestHostToldTheGatewayAddress fails on macOS with a system proxy set (#2562's scutil leak, second test)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Failure

Setup: macOS arm64, origin/main 08982805e, Go 1.26.8, a temporary HOME, Bun 1.4.4 on PATH. The machine has a system proxy set (HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS at 127.0.0.1:7979).

```
$ go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run '^TestHostToldTheGatewayAddress$' ./internal/plugin
    host_addr_test.go:78: after the port moved to 3592 the plugin was told MAGPIE_ADDR=127.0.0.1:3591
--- FAIL: TestHostToldTheGatewayAddress (4.22s)
```

It failed the same way in a full `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -timeout 45m ./...` at c2b8814e7, and on an untouched 9d143eaca.

## Cause

This is the same leak as #2562, in a second test.

- The test sets `proxyLookNone = 0` so that the host looks at its proxy and the gateway's address again at once (`proxyMoved`, `internal/plugin/host.go`).
- That interval only applies to a host started with no proxy. Once `proxied(h.proxy)` is true, `proxyMoved` uses `proxyLookEvery`, 15s.
- The host's proxy is `hostProxy(env())`, and `env()` is `netproxy.Env(os.Environ())`. When neither Settings nor the environment names a proxy, `netproxy.EnvWith` falls back to `System()`, which on macOS runs `scutil --proxy`. `scutil` reads the machine's settings, not the test's HOME.
- With a system proxy set, the host starts with `*_PROXY` set, so it counts as proxied. When the port moves to 3592, it doesn't restart before `told()` reads `MAGPIE_ADDR`.
- `testenv`'s inert tools stand in for `security` and `secret-tool` but not `scutil`, and `internal/plugin`'s `TestMain` runs through `testenv.RunIn`.

## Evidence

Same commit, same machine. The stand-in is a `scutil` first on PATH that prints a dictionary with no proxy. No system setting was changed.

| `scutil` | `TestHostToldTheGatewayAddress` | `TestProxyCheckSaysAProxyPassedBy` (#2562) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| real (proxy at 127.0.0.1:7979) | FAIL, as above | FAIL: `passed by: &{IP: Loc: Ms:584 Error:HTTP 502 Proxied:false}, the proxy asked 0 times` |
| no-proxy stand-in | PASS (0.91s) | PASS (0.05s) |

## Seen before

25 other issues' run records name this test as a red that is already there on the parent, for example #2492, #4063, #4197 and #4917. Some guess at a cause: "port-move timing" (#4456), "port-notification race" (#4065), "port-move flake on this machine" (#4934), and #3978 calls the three reds it names "Bun-, proxy- and port-timing-sensitive". None of them filed it. I haven't checked which of those machines had a system proxy set.

## Fix

The patch on #2562 adds `scutil` to `testenv`'s inert tools. Since `internal/plugin`'s tests go through `testenv`, it should cover this test as well. I haven't run that patch here; the stand-in above is my own.

`TestPluginSOCKSProxy` also failed in these runs, with both `scutil`s. Its error is the `proxyconnect tcp: 502 Bad Gateway: socks connect …` shape from #2207 (Bun 1.4.4 on PATH), so it isn't this leak.

issue.title: claudetui: the trust question and the Bypass Permissions disclaimer are never answered under NO_COLOR (macOS, 0.1.3015), fix on a fork branch

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

macOS (darwin/arm64), magpie 0.1.3015, Claude Code 2.1.311, the account Claude Code itself is signed in to (the default config directory). magpie was running with `NO_COLOR=1` (and `TERM=dumb`) in its environment. I haven't traced where that came from; the process's parent was launchd.

The Claude Code card on Usage › Allowance said the allowance was unavailable, and app.log had this for every `/usage` read and every bridge run:

> Claude Code asked whether to trust /private/var/folders/…/T/magpie-claude-work-501, not answered in the 16.8s its caller waits for it

The last screen the helper reported ended in `❯ ❯ ❯ ❯ …`, one `❯` for each ↓ it pressed.

## Why

`ready()` in `internal/claudetui/tui.go` reads the trust choice from `s.plain()`, the stream with its escapes blanked, and presses Enter only once `❯ Yes, I trust` is the last choice drawn.

- With colors, moving the selection redraws both choice lines, because their colors change, so the words follow `❯` in the stream.
- Under `NO_COLOR` the two choices look the same whether chosen or not, so Claude Code redraws only the pointer cells: a blank where `❯` was and `❯` where the choice goes. This is what a real Claude Code 2.1.311 wrote for one ↓ under `NO_COLOR`, in full:

  ```
  '\x1b(B\x0f\x1b[?2004h\x1b[1D\x1b[4B\r\x1b[1C\x1b[4A \r\x1b[1C\x1b[1B❯\r\r\n\r\n\r\n\x1b[1C\x1b[3A'
  ```

- So the stream never contains `❯ Yes, I trust`. The helper keeps seeing No chosen and presses ↓ once a second until the caller's deadline.

`childEnv` replaces `TERM` but passes `NO_COLOR` through. As far as I can see, only saved accounts get the work folder's trust entry written ahead of time (aab48dea9, from #4830). The default config directory depends on the helper answering the question, so any magpie started with `NO_COLOR` hits this for the signed-in account.

The Bypass Permissions disclaimer, which the same branch of `ready()` answers since 6b4a6dcd4 (#5042), has the same problem. For one ↓ under `NO_COLOR`, a real 2.1.311 wrote:

```
'\x1b[2D\x1b[4B\r\x1b[2C\x1b[4A \r\x1b[2C\x1b[1B❯\r\r\n\r\n\r\n\x1b[2C\x1b[3A'
```

and with colors:

```
'\x1b[2D\x1b[4B\r\x1b[2C\x1b[4A \x1b[5GNo, exit\r\x1b[2C\x1b[1B\x1b[38;5;153m❯\x1b[5GYes, I accept\x1b[39m\r\r\n\r\n\r\n\x1b[2C\x1b[3A'
```

## Fix

One commit on a fork branch, on top of 8bfc551ee:

- Branch: https://github.com/Fldicoahkiin/magpie/tree/fix/trust-choice-no-color
- Compare: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...Fldicoahkiin:magpie:fix/trust-choice-no-color

Changes:

- For both questions, the choice is read off the screen as a terminal shows it (`grid`, `s.looks()`, which the `/usage` panel is already read from) instead of from the stream.
- Nothing else in that branch changes:
  - whether a question is up is still read from the stream since the last clear;
  - ↓ is pressed at most once a second while No is chosen;
  - Enter goes to a Yes that has been shown for 300ms.
- `NO_COLOR` is left as the user set it.
- `docs/subsystems/claude-subscription-bridge.md`: the trust paragraph says the choice is read from the screen and why, and that the disclaimer is answered the same way.
